title: Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity
abstract: Quantum electrodynamics (QED) predicts that the vacuum should behave as a non-linear medium. For many schemes aimed at verifying this fundamental prediction, the signal consists of one or more photons in a certain mode (determined by polarization $σ$ and wave-number $\boldsymbol{k}$) which would be empty in the absence of a QED vacuum non-linearity. Here we consider modifying these schemes by sending in a classical or non-classical (e.g., squeezed) photon state instead of the initial vacuum state in that mode. We find that the detectability can be improved significantly.

bite.hook: Sending classical or non-classical photon states significantly improves the detectability of quantum vacuum non-linearity.
tldr: They investigated modifying schemes for verifying QED vacuum non-linearity by sending in photon states instead of an initial vacuum state.
They considered using classical or non-classical, such as squeezed, photon states in a mode that would normally be empty.
They found that the detectability of the vacuum non-linearity can be improved significantly using this modified approach.
bite.whyItMatters: Proving that the vacuum has non-linear properties is a core prediction of quantum electrodynamics, and better detection schemes bring us closer to observing elusive quantum phenomena.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to spot a faint ripple on a completely still pond by shining a light on it. Instead of leaving the spot dark, the researchers shine a special laser beam into it, making the hidden ripples much easier to see.
